title: The Starting Gate
logline: A foal fears the starting gate opening means time is up, until a mare explains that it means the run can begin.

premise.want: The foal wants to understand the starting gate.
premise.obstacle: The foal doesn't know what the gate opening means.
premise.change: The foal understands that the opening signals a start.

characters.want: To understand why the starting gate opens
To help Foal feel ready to start

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The foal watched the starting gate.

lines.speaker: foal
lines.text: Why does it open? Is our time up?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The foal stepped back from the gate.

lines.speaker: foal
lines.text: Do we have to go home?

lines.speaker: mare
lines.text: No. When it opens, the run can begin.

lines.speaker: foal
lines.text: So it doesn't mean we're too late?

lines.speaker: mare
lines.text: Not at all. It means you can start.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The foal looked at the gate again.

lines.speaker: foal
lines.text: When it opens, I get to run!

lines.action: The gate opens, and the foal steps forward.

lines.speaker: mare
lines.text: That's right. One step, then another.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The foal was ready for the start.

narration: The foal watched the starting gate. Why does it open? Is our time up? The foal stepped back from the gate. Do we have to go home? No. When it opens, the run can begin. So it doesn't mean we're too late? Not at all. It means you can start. The foal looked at the gate again. When it opens, I get to run! That's right. One step, then another. The foal was ready for the start.
